title: Operation Clean Heart
detail: Operation Clean Heart was a nationwide anti-crime drive launched in October 2002 with military deployment under a civilian government. Rights groups reported arrests, deaths in custody, and later legal immunity for security personnel, while official accounts framed the drive as a law-and-order operation.

title: Why it mattered
detail: The operation is important for understanding Bangladesh’s later security-state debates, including militarized policing, legal immunity, custodial death allegations, and the normalization of extraordinary law-and-order measures.

title: Disputed interpretations
detail: Supporters presented the operation as a response to crime and disorder, while human-rights organizations documented alleged abuses and impunity. Casualty and responsibility claims should be attributed to specific sources.
